text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth at 33 weeks of gestation. Social history: N/A

speaker: Patient
text: The newborn is showing signs of respiratory distress including increased respiratory rate, grunting, and retractions. No other system review was mentioned due to the age of the patient. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I must clarify that Tuberculosis is extremely rare in a newborn unless there is known maternal infection or exposure; the symptoms of grunting and retractions are classic for conditions like Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) or Pneumonia. Can you confirm if the mother had any recent infections, and have you been given Vitamin K or surfactant therapy yet? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hyaline Membrane Disease (Respiratory Distress Syndrome).

The chest X-ray showing a fine reticular granulation with a ground-glass appearance is the classic hallmark of HMD due to surfactant deficiency. Given your history of respiratory distress with grunting and retractions, this diagnosis is confirmed. Please ensure the newborn is receiving appropriate surfactant therapy and respiratory support immediately.
